newsitem.title: USA: US W.Coast gasoline jumps four pct on thin supply.
newsitem.headline: US W.Coast gasoline jumps four pct on thin supply.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot gasoline prices jumped four percent Tuesday as traders focused on shortages at supply terminals and a drop in refinery inventories, industry sources said.
CARB unleaded gasoline traded between 75 cents and 76 cents a gallon Tuesday, up three cent from Monday, as it added to a rally that lifted prices 10 percent last week.
The upward move has returned spot prices on the West Coast to their normal four cent premium over the U.S. Gulf, which for several weeks have outstripped PADD 5.
"Things are strong for the (products) outlook," a Northwest refinery trader said.
A key inventory report late Tuesday also gave West Coast markets a boost, as data showed a regional supply down 947,000 barrels last week.
Inventories on the West Coast have fallen to almost four million under year-ago levels.
Exports, agricultural demand, and a handful of partial refinery shutdowns have trimmed inventories, traders said.

Meanwhile, terminals in inland California like San Bernardino and San Diego County were heard falling short of supply Tuesday, traders said. Weeks of poor prices encouraged them to drain inventories and left them unable to handle the sudden price and demand surge, traders said.
On Tuesday, traders said few barrels sold because traders tried time trades, which allow refiners to swap actual barrels for later deliveries, traders said.
"Nobody wants to sell, but everyone want to do time trades," a trader said.
But volumes still remained low, because sellers were reluctant to give it away in a rising market.
In Los Angeles, CARB regular unleaded gasoline rose about 3.00 to 75/76, traders said.
CARB diesel fuel traded between 67/68 cents, a 2.00-cent rise since Monday in Los Angeles.
Conventional gasoline in L.A. jumped 4.00 cents a gallon to 69/71 cents, while jet fuel increased to 61/62 cents amid the increased buying.
